Bambangan.description: Bambangan is a Borneo mango relative with thick skin and fibrous flesh. It is commonly eaten fresh, pickled, or used in traditional dishes.
Bambangan.season: Seasonal or limited availability in Malaysia. Manual verification is recommended for exact peak season.
Bambangan.price: Estimated RM 10.00 – RM 25.00 per kg or processed pack. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Bambangan.uses: Eaten fresh, pickled, or used in traditional Borneo dishes.

Dabai.description: Dabai is a Sarawak fruit with dark purple skin and creamy flesh after softening. It is usually soaked in warm water and eaten with salt or soy sauce.
Dabai.season: Seasonal or limited availability in Malaysia. Manual verification is recommended for exact peak season.
Dabai.price: Estimated RM 16.00 – RM 35.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Dabai.uses: Soaked in warm water and eaten with salt, soy sauce, or rice.

Belimbing Hutan.description: Belimbing Hutan is a lesser-known local fruit with a sour taste. It is usually eaten fresh in small amounts or used in local food preparations.
Belimbing Hutan.season: Seasonal or limited availability in Malaysia. Manual verification is recommended for exact peak season.
Belimbing Hutan.price: Estimated RM 10 – RM 20 per kg. Rare fruit prices may vary depending on location and season.
Belimbing Hutan.uses: Eaten fresh in small amounts or used in local sour preparations.

Terap.description: Terap is a Borneo fruit related to jackfruit with soft sweet flesh. It is usually eaten fresh when ripe.
Terap.season: Seasonal or limited availability in Malaysia. Manual verification is recommended for exact peak season.
Terap.price: Estimated RM 8.00 – RM 25.00 per fruit or kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Terap.uses: Eaten fresh or used in local desserts.

Durian.description: Durian is a well-known Malaysian tropical fruit with a thorny husk and strong aroma. Its rich, creamy flesh is eaten fresh and used in desserts, pastries, and local dishes.
Durian.season: Seasonal in Malaysia. Peak months vary by fruit type, state, and yearly weather; refer to the latest DOA seasonal fruit calendar.
Durian.price: Estimated RM 15.00 – RM 60.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on variety, location, grade, and season.
Durian.uses: Eaten fresh, used in tempoyak, cakes, ice cream, desserts, and pastries.

Manggis.description: Manggis is a seasonal tropical fruit with purple skin and white juicy segments. It has a sweet, slightly tangy taste and is usually eaten fresh.
Manggis.season: Seasonal in Malaysia. Peak months vary by fruit type, state, and yearly weather; refer to the latest DOA seasonal fruit calendar.
Manggis.price: Estimated RM 8.00 – RM 20.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Manggis.uses: Eaten fresh, used in desserts, juices, and fruit salads.

Rambutan.description: Rambutan is a hairy red or yellow fruit with sweet translucent flesh. It is a popular seasonal fruit in Malaysia and is usually eaten fresh.
Rambutan.season: Seasonal in Malaysia. Peak months vary by fruit type, state, and yearly weather; refer to the latest DOA seasonal fruit calendar.
Rambutan.price: Estimated RM 5.00 – RM 15.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Rambutan.uses: Eaten fresh, canned, or used in desserts and fruit salads.

Cempedak.description: Cempedak is a tropical fruit related to jackfruit with yellow, fragrant flesh. The ripe flesh is sweet and commonly eaten fresh or fried as a local snack.
Cempedak.season: Seasonal in Malaysia. Peak months vary by fruit type, state, and yearly weather; refer to the latest DOA seasonal fruit calendar.
Cempedak.price: RM 54.00 per 2–3 kg fruit. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Cempedak.uses: Eaten fresh, fried as a snack, or used in desserts and local kuih.

Belimbing.description: Belimbing is a star-shaped tropical fruit with crisp, juicy flesh and a sweet-sour taste. It is commonly eaten fresh in Malaysia and is also used in juice, rojak, and pickled dishes.
Belimbing.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Belimbing.price: RM 7.00 per 4 pcs. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Belimbing.uses: Eaten fresh, used in juice, rojak, pickles, and local sweet-sour dishes.

Duku.description: Duku is a tropical fruit closely related to langsat and dokong. It has translucent segments with a sweet-sour taste and is commonly eaten fresh.
Duku.season: Seasonal in Malaysia. Peak months vary by fruit type, state, and yearly weather; refer to the latest DOA seasonal fruit calendar.
Duku.price: Estimated RM 8.00 – RM 18.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Duku.uses: Eaten fresh as a seasonal snack.

Langsat.description: Langsat is a small seasonal fruit with translucent flesh and a sweet-sour taste. It is commonly eaten fresh after peeling the thin yellow skin.
Langsat.season: Seasonal in Malaysia. Peak months vary by fruit type, state, and yearly weather; refer to the latest DOA seasonal fruit calendar.
Langsat.price: Estimated RM 8.00 – RM 18.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Langsat.uses: Eaten fresh as a seasonal snack.

Salak.description: Salak is known as snake fruit because of its scaly brown skin. The flesh is firm, crunchy, and sweet-sour, and it is commonly eaten fresh.
Salak.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Salak.price: Estimated RM 8.00 – RM 22.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Salak.uses: Eaten fresh, pickled, or used in rojak and fruit snacks.

Rambai.description: Rambai is a small local fruit with translucent sweet-sour flesh. It is commonly eaten fresh or used in local preserves.
Rambai.season: Seasonal or limited availability in Malaysia. Manual verification is recommended for exact peak season.
Rambai.price: Estimated RM 10.00 – RM 25.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Rambai.uses: Eaten fresh, pickled, or used in preserves and local dishes.

Kuini.description: Kuini is a mango relative with a strong aroma and sweet-sour flesh. It is commonly eaten fresh or used in local desserts and sambal.
Kuini.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Kuini.price: Estimated RM 10.00 – RM 22.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Kuini.uses: Eaten fresh or used in sambal, desserts, juices, and local dishes.

Binjai.description: Binjai is a mango relative with a strong aroma and sour-sweet flesh. It is commonly used in sambal, pickles, and local dishes.
Binjai.season: Seasonal or limited availability in Malaysia. Manual verification is recommended for exact peak season.
Binjai.price: Estimated RM 8 – RM 18 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Binjai.uses: Used in sambal, pickles, and sour local dishes.

Nam-Nam.description: Nam-Nam is a sour tropical fruit with a wrinkled pod-like shape. It is usually eaten with seasoning or used in pickles and local preparations.
Nam-Nam.season: Seasonal or limited availability in Malaysia. Manual verification is recommended for exact peak season.
Nam-Nam.price: Estimated RM 10 – RM 20 per kg. Rare fruit prices may vary depending on location and season.
Nam-Nam.uses: Eaten with seasoning, pickled, or used in sour local preparations.

Kelubi.description: Kelubi is a sour palm fruit found in local wetland areas. It is commonly pickled or used in sour local dishes.
Kelubi.season: Seasonal or limited availability in Malaysia. Manual verification is recommended for exact peak season.
Kelubi.price: Estimated RM 8 – RM 20 per kg or pack. Prices may vary depending on fresh or preserved product form.
Kelubi.uses: Pickled or used in sour local dishes and condiments.

Mata Kucing.description: Mata Kucing is a longan-type fruit with sweet translucent flesh. It is commonly eaten fresh or used in drinks and desserts.
Mata Kucing.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Mata Kucing.price: RM 15.40 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Mata Kucing.uses: Eaten fresh or used in drinks, desserts, and canned fruit products.

Betik.description: Betik is a soft orange-fleshed tropical fruit with a sweet taste when ripe. It is commonly eaten fresh, blended into drinks, or used in desserts and salads.
Betik.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Betik.price: RM 11.30 per medium fruit. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Betik.uses: Eaten fresh, used in salads, smoothies, desserts, and local cooking when unripe.

Jambu Batu.description: Jambu Batu is a crunchy tropical fruit with white or pink flesh and many small seeds. It is rich in vitamin C and commonly eaten fresh or with asam powder.
Jambu Batu.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Jambu Batu.price: RM 10.70 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Jambu Batu.uses: Eaten fresh, used in juice, rojak, salads, and snacks with seasoning.

Jambu Air.description: Jambu Air is a crisp, watery fruit with a mild sweet taste. It is commonly eaten fresh, chilled, or added to fruit salads.
Jambu Air.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Jambu Air.price: Estimated RM 8.00 – RM 18.00 per kg or RM 8.00 – RM 15.00 per pack. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Jambu Air.uses: Eaten fresh, chilled, or used in rojak and fruit salads.

Jambu Air Madu.description: Jambu Air Madu is a sweet wax apple variety with crisp and juicy flesh. It is commonly eaten fresh as a snack.
Jambu Air Madu.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Jambu Air Madu.price: Estimated RM 10.00 – RM 20.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Jambu Air Madu.uses: Eaten fresh, chilled, or used in fruit salads.

Nanas.description: Nanas is a tropical fruit with juicy yellow flesh and a sweet-sour taste. It is eaten fresh, cooked in local dishes, made into juice, or used in desserts.
Nanas.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Nanas.price: RM 6.30 – RM 8.30 per fruit. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Nanas.uses: Eaten fresh, used in juice, rojak, pajeri, curries, desserts, and jams.

Nangka.description: Nangka is a large tropical fruit with sweet yellow bulbs inside. The ripe fruit is eaten fresh, while young jackfruit can be cooked in savoury dishes.
Nangka.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Nangka.price: Estimated RM 6.00 – RM 15.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Nangka.uses: Eaten fresh, used in desserts, curries, young jackfruit dishes, and local snacks.

Pisang.description: Pisang is a common fruit in Malaysia with soft sweet flesh when ripe. It is eaten fresh, fried, steamed, or used in cakes, desserts, and local snacks.
Pisang.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Pisang.price: RM 8.00 – RM 14.20 per kg depending on variety. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Pisang.uses: Eaten fresh, fried, steamed, baked, or used in cakes and desserts.

Longan.description: Longan is a small round fruit with translucent sweet flesh. It is eaten fresh, canned, or used in drinks and desserts.
Longan.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Longan.price: RM 15.40 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Longan.uses: Eaten fresh, canned, or used in drinks and desserts.

Limau Besar.description: Limau Besar, also known as pomelo, is a large citrus fruit with juicy segments. It has a mild sweet-sour taste and is commonly eaten fresh.
Limau Besar.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Limau Besar.price: Estimated RM 5.00 – RM 12.00 per fruit. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Limau Besar.uses: Eaten fresh, used in salads, juices, desserts, and festive dishes.

Tembikai.description: Tembikai is a refreshing fruit with juicy red flesh and high water content. It is eaten fresh, served cold, or blended into juice.
Tembikai.season: Available year-round in Malaysia. Supply may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Tembikai.price: Estimated RM 3.00 – RM 8.00 per kg. Prices may vary depending on location, grade, and season.
Tembikai.uses: Eaten fresh, chilled, juiced, or served in fruit salads.
